report.source_text: An abdominal MRI was conducted, revealing a 58 × 52 × 109 mm intraperitoneal cystic lesion in the right mid to lower abdomen. The inferior margin of the lesion was in close proximity to the caecal pole, thin walled and entirely simple. The interior of the lesion demonstrated T2 hyperintensity but minimal T1 hyperintensity on weighted imaging. The appendix was not identified separate to this lesion as displayed in Fig. 1, Fig. 2. Differential diagnosis included a mesenteric cyst, duplication cyst, and given the appendix was not separately visualized, an appendiceal mucinous lesion.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 33-year-old man presented with lower abdominal pain and fullness following blunt abdominal trauma during a boxing training session. Physical examination revealed a palpable mass in the right lower quadrant. Abdominal MRI on admission identified a 58 × 52 × 109 mm intraperitoneal cystic lesion in the right mid to lower abdomen with the appendix not separately visualized, raising differential diagnosis of appendiceal mucinous lesion. Surgical exploration confirmed a large inflammatory abdominal lesion with enlarged mesenteric lymph nodes and non-visualized appendix. Right hemicolectomy with primary anastomosis was performed. Histopathology confirmed the diagnosis of completely excised low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasm with fifteen negative lymph nodes. The patient had an unremarkable long-term postoperative course with full return to baseline functioning.
